title: How do we draw a parallel line through a point?
description: A line m and a point B off it are given. A transversal through B, the angle at A copied at B in the matching corner, and the line through B and E give a parallel line, justified by side side side. Keeko's doubt, marking E on the other side, is tested and struck out.
teaching_notes: One idea: copy the corresponding angle, and equal corresponding angles make parallel lines. Watch for students who mark E on the wrong side of the transversal.

source: A line m and a point B not on it are given. Construct a line parallel to m through B.
video_script.why: The child can copy an angle but has not yet used the copy to make a parallel line.
video_script.substitution: Equal corresponding angles give parallel lines, so copying one angle gives the parallel line.
video_script.anchor: A line m and a point B off it: draw the line through B parallel to m, using only a ruler and a compass.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko marks E on the other side of the transversal. The copied angle then sits in the wrong corner, and the line through B and E slants and meets m.
video_script.payoff_line: The line n is parallel to m

final_answer.value: The line n through B and E, since the copied corresponding angles are equal (SSS), so n ∥ m
final_answer.spoken: the line n through B and E is parallel to m, because the corresponding angles are equal by side side side

never_show: the finished line n before step three
maths_rules: Line l through B cuts m at A; l is the transversal.
An arc with centre A cuts m at C and l at D, between A and B: AC = AD.
The same radius with centre B cuts l at F, beyond B, away from A: BF = AD, and every point E on this arc has BE = AC.
The compass is set to CD; with centre F it cuts the arc at E, on the same side of l as C: FE = DC.
Triangle BFE is congruent to triangle ADC by SSS, so angle FBE = angle DAC. These are corresponding angles on the transversal l, so n through B and E is parallel to m.
Slip: E on the other side of l gives the angle in the opposite corner, and the line through B and E is not parallel to m.
video_script.design: One idea: copy the corresponding angle. It assumes copying an angle. Keeko's doubt is E on the other side of the transversal. The book's figure for the point labels is garbled, so the labels follow the worklist.
open_questions: The extracted book figure is garbled, so the positions of C, D, F and E follow the worklist and the matching corners are worked out from the maths.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A line that crosses other lines is called a transversal.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Angles in matching corners are called corresponding angles.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>If corresponding angles are equal, the two lines are parallel.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, draw a line l through B that cuts m at eigh. This is the transversal.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Put the compass point on eigh, and draw an arc with any radius.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>It cuts m at C, and it cuts l at D, between eigh and B.

marks.m1: the compass keeps its opening and moves to B
marks.m2: an arc from B cuts l at F, beyond B, away from eigh

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, keep the same radius, and put the compass point on B.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Draw an arc that cuts l at F, beyond B, away from eigh.

marks.m2: from F it cuts the arc at E, on the same side of l as C

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, open the compass to the length C D.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Put the point on F, and cut the arc at E. Keep E on the same side of l as C. Then F E equals C D.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Draw the line n through B and E.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: triangles BFE and ADC: BF = AD, BE = AC, FE = DC; SSS gives angle FBE = angle DAC, a pair of corresponding angles

marks.m1: the triangles B F E and eigh D C are shaded
marks.m2: the three pairs of equal sides light up
marks.m3: the corners at B and eigh get matching arcs

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, look at triangles B F E and eigh D C.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>B F equals eigh D, B E equals eigh C, and F E equals D C. By side side side, they are congruent.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Then angle F B E equals angle D eigh C. These are corresponding angles, and they are equal.

beats.on_screen: Answer: n is parallel to m, because the corresponding angles are equal by SSS
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The line n is parallel to m.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The copied corresponding angles are equal, by side side side.
